name: MOLDOVA

flag.title: Blue, Yellow & Red
flag.note: Eagle on yellow holds a cross & shield

lead: Moldova is a tiny country between Romania and Ukraine, smaller than Ireland. Cave tunnels carved from limestone hold millions of wine bottles. Farmers have made wine here for 5,000 years. Now it looks toward the EU.
geo: Moldova is one of Europe's flattest countries. It has gentle hills and wide valleys cut by the Prut and the Dniester. Black soil called chernozem makes fine farmland.
Oak and hornbeam forests cover the central Codru hills, sheltering deer and wild boar. Moldova has no sea coast at all.
animals: The white stork is Moldova's national bird. Thousands nest on chimneys every spring, and a stork on your roof is good luck.
The European mink is a small, chestnut-furred creature that slides through reeds. It is critically endangered, but it clings on in the Prut River floodplains.
culture: Moldovans love to dance. The hora is a whirling circle dance at every wedding and harvest feast. Villagers still make woven rugs and embroidered blouses by hand.
Wine is the heart of Moldovan life. Every October, the whole country celebrates National Wine Day with open cellars and folk music. A Soviet-era limestone quarry became a huge underground wine city.
history: Stephen the Great ruled from 1457 to 1504 and won 34 of his 36 battles against the Ottomans. After every victory he built a monastery. Dozens still stand.
Moldova became Soviet in 1940. On 27 August 1991, as the USSR crumbled, it declared independence. On 25 June 2024, it opened EU accession talks.
wows: Mileștii Mici holds over 1.5 million wine bottles, a world record.
Its 55 km of wine tunnels are so big that visitors drive through them.
Vines cover roughly 4% of Moldova's land, among the highest shares anywhere.
Monks carved the cave monastery at Orheiul Vechi into a limestone cliff over 600 years ago.
Money sent home from abroad equals roughly 12% of Moldova's economy.
Moldova opened EU accession talks on 25 June 2024.
White storks fly from Africa each year to the same chimney.

myths.myth: White wine is made from white grapes only
myths.fact: Grape juice is clear. Red wine gets its colour from the skins. Removing the skins quickly makes white wine from red grapes.
Only young sunflowers turn with the sun. Once grown, they face east and stay put.
